description: Thirteen gene symbols were silently turned into dates when the table passed through a spreadsheet: SEPT2 became '2-Sep', MARCH1 became '1-Mar', DEC1 became '1-Dec', and so on. Because MARCH1 and MARC1 both became '1-Mar', gene_symbol even has fewer unique values than there are rows. value_counts() or simply sorting the column puts the dates right at the top. This is the real Excel gene-name bug: a 2016 study by Ziemann, Eren and El-Osta in Genome Biology found it in roughly a fifth of genomics papers with Excel gene lists, and in 2020 the HGNC renamed the SEPT and MARCH genes (to SEPTIN and MARCHF) partly to stop it. The dataset here is synthetic, inspired by that bug.
hints: Each row should be a different gene. Check whether every text column really is what its description says.
Look closely at the gene symbols: compare nunique() with the row count, and sort them.
Some gene symbols read '1-Mar', '2-Sep' or '1-Dec'. A spreadsheet turned MARCH1, SEPT2 and DEC1 into dates.
